layers.hydrograph-rivers: Every river stretch from the hydrology graph, coloured by kind (flat / sloped / waterfall), width by size band (creek, stream, river); a channel or rapid shorter than 30 m is absorbed into its neighbour so seams stay few; white arrowheads point downstream, white dots are confluences, white rings are mouths.
layers.hydrograph-bodies: Standing water from the graph, coloured by kind: lakes, tarns, ponds, pools, plunge pools, and the marsh sheets.
layers.hydrograph-season: Blue = holds water all year (perennial); orange = dries out in the dry season (seasonal). Once a river is perennial it stays so to its mouth.
layers.hydrograph-falls: Waterfalls measured on the base terrain (red-ringed discs) and their plunge pools (blue dots).
layers.hydrograph-wetline: The wet-season high-water extent: the Phase 3 wetlands + rivers + lakes footprint.

horizontal-channel.name: horizontal-channel
horizontal-channel.about: A flat river stretch: the water level falls less than 3.5 cm per metre. Its size is the band (1 creek, 2 stream, 3 river, by catchment 1 / 4 / 15 km2), drawn as line width; one surface for the renderer whatever the band.

horizontal-backwater.name: horizontal-backwater
horizontal-backwater.about: The river passing through a lake or pond: these stations sit inside a standing body and take its level.

horizontal-tidal.name: horizontal-tidal
horizontal-tidal.about: A flat stretch within reach of the tide: most of it lies in the tidal mask (under 1.5 m and salty).

sloped-riffle.name: sloped-riffle
sloped-riffle.about: A gently sloping run: the water level falls 3.5 to 6.5 cm per metre. Fast, shallow, gravelly.

sloped-rapid.name: sloped-rapid
sloped-rapid.about: A rapid: the level falls 6.5 to 50 cm per metre. Whitewater over boulders.

sloped-chute.name: sloped-chute
sloped-chute.about: A steep slide: the level falls more than 50 cm per metre but the rock face is under 70 degrees, so the water runs on it rather than leaving it.

vertical-fall.name: vertical-fall
vertical-fall.about: A waterfall: a drop of 3 m or more over a face steeper than 70 degrees.

ocean.name: ocean
ocean.about: Sea-connected water below sea level that the coarse pass calls open ocean.

lagoon.name: lagoon
lagoon.about: Sea-connected water below sea level that winds inland beyond the open-ocean reach.

lake-lowland.name: lake-lowland
lake-lowland.about: Standing water of 1 hectare or more whose level is under 30 m.

tarn-upland.name: tarn-upland
tarn-upland.about: Standing water of 1 hectare or more whose level is 30 m or higher (an upland or mountain lake).

pond.name: pond
pond.about: Standing water between 500 m2 and 1 hectare.

plunge-pool.name: plunge-pool
plunge-pool.about: The pool a waterfall lands in.

marsh-fringe.name: marsh-fringe
marsh-fringe.about: A flat wet sheet in the fringe-marsh or coastal-marsh region classes.

marsh-deep.name: marsh-deep
marsh-deep.about: A flat wet sheet in the rootland deep-marsh region class, or any sheet over 0.5 m deep.

swamp.name: swamp
swamp.about: A flat wet sheet in the interior-swamp region class (forested, seasonally flooded).

backswamp.name: backswamp
backswamp.about: A flat wet sheet on the seasonal floodplain, beyond a river's levee.

mudflat.name: mudflat
mudflat.about: A flat tidal sheet in the delta region class.

perennial.name: perennial
perennial.about: Holds water all year. A body is perennial unless the dry-season draw-down (a fifth of the 1.4 m season swing, scaled by the body's response) empties it; a river stretch is perennial from the first point its catchment reaches 4 km2 or it enters the marsh heartland, and stays so downstream.

seasonal.name: seasonal
seasonal.about: Dries out in the dry season: a shallow sheet the draw-down empties, or a headwater creek above the perennial point.

ephemeral.name: ephemeral
ephemeral.about: Flows only after rain (not used on this province yet).

fall.name: waterfall
fall.about: A measured drop of 3 m or more where the ground face is steeper than 70 degrees, so water leaves the rock. Red ring, white disc.

plunge.name: plunge pool
plunge.about: The pool at the foot of a waterfall, dug by it; promised for 16b to dig where the base has none.

wet.name: wet-season high-water extent
wet.about: The Phase 3 wetlands, rivers and lakes footprint, declared the wet-season high-water line (owner, 2026-09-11).
